name: lance_file::benches::reader::bench_reader
behavior: bench_reader iterates exact V2_0,V2_1,V2_2 (no V1 or V2_3), creates reader_{version} group, generates one random Int32 column with2*1024*1024=2097152 rows and no requested random-null wrapper, creates Runtime::new and a temporary local object store. All generation/runtime/directory/store construction occurs outside b.iter; failures unwrap. Group spelling uses ConcreteFileVersion Display. Untimed setup writes foo.lance once using actual Arrow schema converted to Lance and default file-writer options, then awaits write_batch and finish. Throughput::Bytes is input RecordBatch::get_array_memory_size cast to u64, not persisted file length or bytes actually read. No input expected sum is precomputed. Timed decode b.iter includes Runtime::block_on, a fresh ScanScheduler with testing config, unknown-size open_file, FileReader::try_open with default plugins, a newly created test_cache and default options, then RangeFull read_tasks with batch size16384, no projection and no filter. Thus the name decode includes opening, metadata/scheduling/cache setup and IO, not only decompression. test_cache requests128MiB; testing scheduler config requests256MiB buffer and use_lite_scheduler=None (rust/lance-file/src/testing.rs:78-80; rust/lance-io/src/scheduler.rs:861-865). There is no OS page-cache eviction in this workload. Each timed scan wraps row_count and i64 sum in Arc<Mutex>, maps batch tasks to boxed futures, awaits up to16 unordered, scans underlying Int32 values (not validity-aware iterator), accumulates count/sum under lock, and drains all tasks. Assert total rows equals original2097152 and black_box sum; no sum equality or full-data/null correctness check. Assertion and synchronization/consumption costs are timed. No RecordBatch collection is retained. End of all-version scan loop.
callees: Datagen; Runtime; ObjectStore; versions::create_writer; ScanScheduler; FileReader::read_tasks; buffered task consumption; Criterion.

name: lance_file::benches::reader::drop_file_from_cache
behavior: Non-Linux cfg defines pub drop_file_from_cache(path:impl AsRef<std::path::Path>)->std::io::Result<()> as unconditional Ok; ignores path and performs no file access or cache eviction. Pub is visibility inside benchmark executable, not a lance_file export. The later nocache label therefore does not prove cold disk IO on these platforms.
callees: Immediate Ok, no IO.

name: lance_file::benches::reader::drop_file_from_cache
behavior: Linux alternative opens the supplied path, borrows its live file descriptor and unsafely calls libc::posix_fadvise(fd,0,0,POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED). Comment identifies constant4 and intent to drop pages. No raw pointer/buffer is passed; File stays alive through call. There is no SAFETY comment, fsync, post-advice residency check or guarantee the advisory request removes every cache. Nonzero returned error number is converted directly with from_raw_os_error; open/advice failures return Err, then caller unwraps. File drops afterward. This call was not executed.
callees: File::open; AsRawFd; unsafe libc::posix_fadvise; from_raw_os_error.

name: lance_file::benches::reader::get_cached_readers
behavior: get_cached_readers borrows TempDir, filesystem label and Runtime and accepts exact version. A function-local static LazyLock<Mutex<FileCache>> lazily creates a process-wide cache. Key is filesystem.to_string plus version.to_string; it excludes directory path, CPU count, options and row grouping. Hit clones Arc under lock and returns. Lock poison panics. Miss releases lookup lock before expensive creation, so concurrent misses are not coalesced and later insert can replace prior cached entry. Current benchmark caller invokes setup sequentially. On miss determine compute count T via cached get_num_compute_intensive_cpus. Label exactly mem creates memory:// store; every other string uses the supplied temporary path. Filename is bench_{version}.lance ONLY; filesystem is in cache key/store choice, contrary to comment claiming both filesystem and version in filename. Current mem/disk stores keep active cases separate; arbitrary other labels sharing a directory are not isolated by filename. CPU helper clamps fallback to1, honors LANCE_CPU_THREADS>=1 or CPU count minus LANCE_IO_CORE_RESERVATION default2, caches its result and panics on invalid explicit numeric text (rust/lance-core/src/utils/tokio.rs:12-76). Untimed miss setup materializes one Int32 column of500*1024*1024=524288000 rows with requested random-null probability0.1, creates/writes/finishes a versioned file with default options. Requested raw Int32 payload is2097152000 bytes (2000MiB), plus a potential65536000-byte validity bitmap and other allocation/encoding overhead; these are arithmetic size estimates, not measured peak RSS, exact null count or encoded file size. Full batch stays alive while writer/readers warm up, then leaves helper scope. No streaming fixture generation is used. Create100000 UInt32 selectors i*5120, first0,last511994880, all below524288000 fixture rows. This is a deterministic strided access pattern, not random selector generation. Compute rows_per_thread=floor(100000/T), allocate T CachedReader slots and slice contiguous equal chunks, dropping division remainder from per-thread slices while preserving full all_indices separately. Build one current-thread Runtime per slice without enable_all/enable_io/enable_time calls; runtime/scheduler compatibility is delegated, not executed here. Open each per-thread reader and warm it with read_task rows_at_a_time100 outside timing, then retain reader/indices/runtime. Warmup itself discards incomplete groups through read_task floor division. Wrap all readers/full selectors in Arc, lock cache again and insert/reassign key. Static cache retains readers/stores/runtimes for process lifetime without retaining TempDir; future cache hits with another directory can reuse stale file paths after directory cleanup. No explicit cache invalidation/reset or cleanup hook is defined.
callers: bench_random_access before each store/version case registration.
callees: Static cache lock; CPU sizing; ObjectStore; datagen; versioned writer; UInt32 selectors; current-thread Runtime; open_reader; read_task warmup.

name: lance_file::benches::reader::open_reader
behavior: open_reader block_on creates a new testing scheduler, opens unknown file size, opens FileReader with no projection, default decoder plugins, fresh128MiB test cache, and a redundantly explicit DecoderConfig default inside FileReaderOptions default. Returns Arc reader and unwraps all failures. Every cached worker reader has separate cache/scheduler construction. Neither method clears OS pages nor disables Lance caches (rust/lance-file/src/testing.rs:78-80; rust/lance-io/src/scheduler.rs:861-865).

name: lance_file::benches::reader::read_task
behavior: read_task receives Runtime reference, owned reader Arc, UInt32Array and rows_at_a_time. Capture total selector length. Its local read_batch closure calls read_tasks with Indices, rows_at_a_time cast to u32, no projection/filter, awaits creation and allocates a fresh Arc<Mutex<(row_count,sum)>> per selector chunk. No nonzero/u32-range input validation is local; active call sites use1 or100. Within each selector chunk, stream.then awaits each batch task sequentially, sums the raw Int32 values buffer including backing values under null slots, locks aggregate, and drains all output. Assert only rows_at_a_time equals decoded row count; black_box sum without comparing expected values/nulls. Returns unit. This is a consumption anti-elision operation, not a correctness oracle for values or null placement. Runtime block_on enumerates0..floor(num_rows/rows_at_a_time), clones reader and selector handles, slices exact-size contiguous chunks, and awaits up toMAX_PARALLELISM64 chunk futures unordered. Final collect::<Vec<_>>() retains unit results, not RecordBatch payloads. Remainder selectors are silently unprocessed; zero group size would divide by zero. No outer assertion compares consumed rows to original selector length. Per-call decoded count is rows_at_a_time*floor(num_rows/rows_at_a_time).
callers: get_cached_readers warmup and both timed random-access thread modes.
callees: Local read_batch closure; Runtime::block_on; selector slicing; buffer_unordered64.

name: lance_file::benches::reader::bench_random_access
behavior: bench_random_access defines filesystems[mem,disk], one current-thread global runtime without enable_all and one TempDir, creates take group, and chooses V2_0,V2_1,V2_2 only. Current runtime handles spawn_blocking coordination, while cached per-reader current-thread runtimes execute read_task. No direct benchmark-specific environment lookup in this file; CPU/env effects enter the helper. For each store/version get cached readers before registering cases. Cartesian loops choose multithreaded false/true, rows_at_a_time1/100 and cached true/false, skipping nocache for mem or V2_0. Nominal32 random-access registrations:12mem and20disk; if compute T=1 both thread-mode names coincide, and duplicate-name handling is Criterion-dependent/unverified. Active multithread uses cached compute count T, otherwise1. Throughput Elements advertises T*floor(100000/T); it does not account for later rows_at_a_time truncation. Actual parallel count is T*g*floor(floor(100000/T)/g), where g is1 or100; single-thread uses full100000 selectors, divisible by both active g. Benchmark name formats filesystem_version_{num_threads}thread_{rows_at_a_time}_{cached|nocache}. iter_batched setup closure optionally constructs absolute temporary filename bench_{version}.lance and redundantly joins it to tempdir again, then invokes drop_file_from_cache and unwraps. This is the Criterion setup closure, separate from timed routine; no direct local timer surrounds advice. It does not recreate cached readers or clear Lance caches. On non-Linux the helper is a no-op; on Linux it only requests advisory eviction. Timed routine clones cached Arc and block_on global runtime. Multithread branch allocates join-handle Vec, iterates cached worker readers, clones each runtime/indices/reader and spawn_blocking one read_task per worker, then awaits handles in launch order with unwrap. All tasks launch before joins; inner calls each allow64 concurrent chunks, so at most64*T chunk futures can be active across workers, independent of decoder-internal parallelism. Timing includes task dispatch/join/Arc clones and consumption. Single-thread branch still spawn_blocking, using reader0/runtime0 but full all_indices rather than worker0 slice, then awaits one handle. No direct bound on Tokio blocking pool size is configured here. BatchSize::PerIteration requests one setup per timed iteration; comment claiming at least0.1s work is rationale, not measured evidence. Function exits loops and lets local TempDir/global runtime drop, while static cached Arcs remain; there is no explicit group.finish in this function.
callees: get_cached_readers; CPU sizing; Criterion iter_batched; drop_file_from_cache; global runtime spawn_blocking/read_task.

name: lance_file::benches::reader::benches
behavior: Linux criterion_group benches uses Criterion default overridden to significance_level0.1 and sample_size10 plus PProfProfiler::new(100,Output::Flamegraph(None)); profiler parameter interpretation is delegated. Non-Linux omits profiler but uses same significance/sample settings. Both target bench_reader and bench_random_access; criterion_main!(benches) supplies entry point. No explicit warmup/measurement duration or standalone test module. Cargo registers reader with harness=false (rust/lance-file/Cargo.toml:63-65).
callees: Criterion default significance0.1/sample10; PProfProfiler new100/Flamegraph(None); both benchmarks.

name: lance_file::benches::schema::wide_two_leaf_structs
behavior: wide_two_leaf_structs asserts even num_physical_columns, divides by2 for root count, and reserves root+leaf field capacity. Parameter names physical columns mean leaves, not total protobuf entries; each root adds another entry. Zero is accepted and returns an empty Fields wrapper. There is no checked capacity arithmetic or general usize-to-i32 range bound. For root indexi assign parent ID(3*i) cast to i32, root parent_id-1/name struct_i/logical struct, then leaves IDsparent+1/parent+2 namesleft_i/right_i logical int32 and parent_id equal root. Emit exact pre-order parent,left,right; consumes3 IDs per struct. Arithmetic/casts are unchecked for arbitrary huge inputs. Active leaf counts below keep IDs in range. Returns Fields(Vec<pb::Field>) without separately validating fixture shape.
callees: Even-count assertion; Vec allocation; proto_field three times per root.

name: lance_file::benches::schema::bench_schema_reconstruction
behavior: bench_schema_reconstruction creates group schema_from_flat_fields; four leaf counts1024,4096,16384,65536 create512,2048,8192,32768 roots and total1536,6144,24576,98304 flat entries. Fixture building occurs once per case outside timed closure. Throughput::Elements uses fields.0.len, hence ALL root+leaf entries, while parameter is physical leaf count. bench_with_input names each case physical_columns/<leaf count> and borrows prebuilt Fields. Timed bencher.iter calls Schema::try_from(black_box(fields)).unwrap(), returning the new schema to Criterion. Measures reconstruction/allocation from parsed messages, not decoding protobuf bytes or fixture generation. No equality, shape, performance-threshold or memory assertion follows; Criterion owns result handling. Explicit group.finish closes registration.
callees: wide_two_leaf_structs; Criterion::bench_with_input; black_box; Schema::try_from.
